sources.citation: Ruckstuhl, Christoph. 1998 [2007 file]. Phonology of Gbaya of Bossangoa (SIL CAR) + Samarin, William J. 1966. The Gbeya Language (UCPL 44) -- sister language gbay1287, already in catalog
sources.note: For Gbeya (not Bokoto): 'Gbaya has no phonemic stress' (Ruckstuhl sec. 5.2 p.24); Samarin lists stress only among non-structured 'stylistically utilized vocal modifiers' (fn. 21). Context only; different glottocode.

sources.citation: Blühberger, Jutta. 2019 [rédigé 1994]. Rapport d'enquête sociolinguistique: première évaluation parmi les Bokoto. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2019-008. iv+29 pp. SIL archives entry 83988.
sources.note: Nothing; sociolinguistic survey (dialects, intercomprehension, Sango bilingualism), classification after Moñino 1988; 'accents' used only for regional dialect accents.

sources.citation: Boyd, Ginger, en collaboration avec Etienne Ngaibele, Célestin Paimo et Edouard Koya. 2015 [2021 printing]. Précis d'orthographe Bhogoto. ACATBA et SIL International (SIL RCA). 25 pp. SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 64835.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3 (p.2) syllable and word shapes; sec. 6 'Les tons' (p.13-15): two underlying tones H/L, predictable surface super-high from H-spread or blocking by depressor consonants (b d g gb v z), nouns/prepositions lexically toned, verbs toneless with grammatical (aspect/mood) melodies; the words accent/stress/intensité/proéminence never occur in a prosodic sense (only 'accent aigu/grave' as tone diacritics).

sources.citation: Huntley, Adam. 2015. Les observations du système tonal en langue Bhogoto (Observations on the Tone System in Bhogoto). Draft ms., 8 pp. SIL Language & Culture Archives 73209.

sources.note: First-hand SIL tone analysis of Bhogoto from the 2015 tone-orthography workshop; may comment on stress/prominence vs tone; archived but 'Not Available Online' (request from SIL CAR / archives@sil.org).
